title: Regional capacity playbook — Q3/Q4 2026
body:
Purpose:
This working playbook consolidates regional GPU capacity sizing, utilization targets, and the phased rollout timeline for NA / EU / APAC for Q3–Q4 2026. Intended audience: infra planners, release engineering, SRE, and solutions engineering.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We expect demand growth driven by Hosted API peak seasonality and 2 large Dedicated deals that target EU and APAC. To meet SLOs while keeping cost/margin visibility, plan to expand committed capacity and burst pools across three cloud regions (NA-west, EU-central, APAC-sg). Targeted addition = 1,200 usable accelerators July–Dec 2026, with an operational buffer of 20% (hot spare + capacity for canary rollouts). This doc defines monthly targets, assumptions, rollout phases, and open risks.

Assumptions (hard):
- Primary instance types: H100-80GB (production-critical), A100-40GB (economy/backfill). New fleet purchases targeted at H100 where customer latency demands >25ms p50 for 2k token sequences.
- Average customer workload mix: 65% short-chat, 25% long-completion, 10% embeddings/batch.
- Target steady-state utilization: 70% p95 (i.e., provision for 30% headroom).
- Autoscaler will maintain baseline capacity + burst pool; burst policy triggered at 85% sustained.
- Exchange rate / cloud price trends: assume 5% price drift for EU/APAC in modeling window.

Sizing table (usable accelerators by month) — values are usable GPUs after accounting for node overheads and reserve pool:

Month, NA (H100/A100 split), EU (H100/A100 split), APAC (H100/A100 split), Total usable GPUs
2026-07, NA: 420 (300/120), EU: 240 (160/80), APAC: 120 (80/40), Total: 780
2026-08, NA: 520 (380/140), EU: 300 (200/100), APAC: 140 (100/40), Total: 960
2026-09, NA: 620 (450/170), EU: 380 (250/130), APAC: 180 (120/60), Total: 1,180
2026-10, NA: 720 (520/200), EU: 420 (300/120), APAC: 200 (140/60), Total: 1,340
2026-11, NA: 780 (560/220), EU: 460 (320/140), APAC: 220 (150/70), Total: 1,460
2026-12, NA: 820 (590/230), EU: 500 (350/150), APAC: 250 (170/80), Total: 1,570

Notes on table: numbers include a 20% operational buffer (hot and warm spares). H100/A100 split guidance is conservative: we bias H100 in NA and EU due to higher latency and throughput demand; APAC uses a slightly higher proportion of A100 to reduce cost while keeping latency within SLOs.

Regional rollout phases (phasing plan with checkpoints):
- Phase 0 (planning) — Mar–May 2026: finalize procurement & cloud credits, open orders, land budget approvals (owner: Maya). Checkpoint: purchase orders submitted + cloud quota requests in place.
- Phase 1 (NA expansion) — Jun–Aug 2026: deploy NA-west pool + enable routing for new Dedicated customers. Checkpoint: NA p50 latency < target for canary traffic and canary customers onboarded.
- Phase 2 (EU ramp) — Aug–Oct 2026: expand EU-central capacity to support two enterprise rollouts; enable cross-region fallback from NA. Checkpoint: EU canary success, SLA runbook validated.
- Phase 3 (APAC readiness) — Sep–Dec 2026: staged APAC additions, begin Dedicated placement for APAC pilot customers in Oct. Checkpoint: APAC latency/p95 observed below regional SLO in load tests.

Routing & traffic policies during rollout:
- Canary traffic: 2% of production traffic routed to new nodes for 72 hours with synthetic and real-user checks.
- Fallback policy: if p95 latency exceeds SLO on new pool for >30m, route new requests to nearest compatible pool and auto-scale burst up to 30% in origin region.
- Cost-aware routing: non-critical batch workloads preferentially routed to A100 pools; H100 reserved for latency-sensitive endpoints.

Utilization targets and monitoring signals:
- Target steady-state: 70% avg usable-GPU utilization across each region with 30% headroom (measured over 30d windows).
- Warmup threshold: when utilization reaches 65% for 6h continuous, trigger pre-provision scale event (automated) and alert on call.
- Alert signals: sustained p95 latency above SLO, queue-length growth > 30rd percentile baseline, KV-cache eviction rate > target.

Capacity economics (high-level):
- Expected incremental committed monthly spend Jul–Dec = $2.1M (cloud + instance discounts assumed).
- Unit economics: targeted amortized GPU cost (cloud + infra) = $1.9–2.4k / GPU / month depending on reserved vs on-demand mix.
- Key levers to reduce cost: increase A100 share in non-latency tiers, more aggressive prefix caching, and centralized batch pools for embeddings.

Operational playbook (actions, owners, ETA):
- Confirm pre-orders and quotas for all three clouds (owner: Diego, ETA: 2026-03-20).
- Create regional canary checklist and automated test harness (owner: Ava, ETA: 2026-05-01).
- Update routing policy codex and release gating (owner: Liam, ETA: 2026-05-15).
- Cost runbook for burst events (owner: Sofia, ETA: 2026-06-01).

Open questions / risks (notes-to-self):
- Procurement lead times may shift: H100 shipment windows uncertain — build contingency of +6 weeks.
- EU data residency/contract approvals could delay Dedicated rollouts by 2–4 weeks. Flag sales to adjust timelines.
- If cloud spot market volatility increases, on-demand fallback could spike costs; need automated budget guardrails.

Quick test matrix (what to run during canary):
- Latency smoke: 5000 synthetic short-chat requests (2–4 tokens) + 200 long-depth completions (1500–2k tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 500 concurrent streams over 2h to validate batching behavior.
- Regression checks: output-quality evals (subset prompts) vs baseline model run to detect perf regressions.

Appendix: short FAQs & references
- Why 20% buffer? Empirically reduces incident-triggered cold starts and supports rollouts without impacting customers.
- How to change H100/A100 split? Route change requires infra config + release gating and a 48h canary.

Links and related tickets (work in progress):
- INFRA-4123: regional quota requests
- INFRA-4310: routing policy changes for cost-aware placement
- PR 289: initial infra templates for regional pools

Immediate next steps (today):
- Sync with procurement on PO timelines (Maya)
- Kick off canary harness issues in GitHub (Ava)
- Share this draft with Release Eng and Solutions Eng for inputs (Diego)

-- end of draft playbook --

Status notes: this is an iterative, working sheet. Expect many updates: move to final by 2026-05-30 after procurement and canary harness are green.
